skill.name: process-code-review
skill.description: Process severity-tagged code review findings through an interactive workflow that fixes, skips, checks, and records each issue.
skill.summary: Turns severity-tagged code review documents into a tracked fix, skip, check, and status update workflow.
skill.author: DiversioTeam

security_audit.summary: All 42 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, slash-command examples, and documented quality-check commands. No prompt injection, secret access, network exfiltration, or hidden executable code was found in SKILL.md. The main residual risk is workflow-level: auto mode can apply changes from untrusted review documents.

remediation.issue: Auto mode can apply review-driven fixes without per-issue confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to use auto mode only with trusted review documents and to preview target files before editing.

remediation.issue: Review document content can steer file edits.
remediation.suggestion: Require source-context review, path validation, and a diff check before accepting proposed fixes from a review document.

static_findings.snippet: - After running `/monty-code-review:code-review` to generate a review document.
- When you have a `*_review.md` file with severity-tagged issues to process.
- `python manage.py check` - Django system checks (if applicable)
| `--dry-run` | Show all issues and proposed fixes without modifying any files |
| `--auto` | Apply all fixes without prompting (use with caution) |
| `--severity=<LEVEL>` | Filter to only process issues of specified severity |
- `--auto --severity=NIT`: Auto-fix only NITs (safe for minor style fixes)

semantic_findings.title: Automated Review Processing Can Apply Untrusted Changes
semantic_findings.description: The skill reads review documents, extracts proposed fixes, and supports auto mode for applying fixes without prompting. A malicious or untrusted review document could steer source edits if the user runs auto mode.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented workflow lets review-file content drive source edits, and auto mode removes per-issue prompts. Risk is limited because the user must invoke the skill and the documented commands are project checks.

content.value_statement: Code review documents can leave teams with a long, hard-to-track fix list. This skill turns those findings into an ordered workflow for fixes, skips, checks, and status updates.
actual_capabilities: Parses review documents with BLOCKING, SHOULD_FIX, and NIT severity tags.
Creates a TodoWrite list that tracks each issue through completion.
Presents findings in priority order for fix or skip decisions.
Applies accepted fixes and updates review documents with status markers.
Runs documented checks such as ruff, ty, and Django checks when applicable.
limitations: Designed for review documents that follow the expected Markdown structure.
Requires project tools such as ruff or ty before related checks can run.
Auto mode can change many files and should be limited to trusted review documents.
Does not commit changes; a separate pre-commit workflow is expected.

use_cases.title: Resolve Generated Review Findings
use_cases.description: Work through a generated review document, fix accepted issues, and keep the review file updated.

use_cases.title: Triage Team Review Debt
use_cases.description: Review a teammate review file, skip unsuitable fixes with reasons, and preserve an audit trail.

use_cases.title: Verify Blocking Issues
use_cases.description: Focus on high-priority findings first and confirm that security or correctness problems are addressed.

prompt_templates.title: Process a Review File
prompt_templates.prompt: Use process-code-review on docs/code_reviews/service_review.md and walk me through each finding interactively.

prompt_templates.title: Preview Before Editing
prompt_templates.prompt: Run process-code-review in dry-run mode on api_review.md. Summarize findings by severity without changing files.

prompt_templates.title: Focus on Blocking Issues
prompt_templates.prompt: Process only BLOCKING findings in payments_review.md. Ask before each fix and update the review document status.

prompt_templates.title: Automate Trusted Cleanup
prompt_templates.prompt: For a trusted generated review file, process NIT findings automatically, run available checks, and summarize modified files.

output_examples.input: Process a review document with three blocking issues and two minor cleanup items.
output: A severity-ordered work list with every finding tracked.
A fix or skip decision prompt for each issue.
A completion summary with fixed, skipped, and modified-file counts.

output_examples.input: Preview a review file before editing source files.
output_examples.output: A grouped dry-run summary that lists findings by severity and confirms no files were changed.

output_examples.input: Apply trusted minor cleanup findings and run checks.
output: Minor findings are processed in order.
Available lint, format, type, and project checks are reported.
The review document records updated status for processed items.

best_practices: Use interactive mode for unfamiliar or externally supplied review documents.
Read source context before accepting proposed fixes from the review document.
Run quality gates after each meaningful change and record skipped reasons.
anti_patterns: Running auto mode on untrusted review documents.
Treating proposed fixes as authoritative without checking current source code.
Marking issues fixed before tests or relevant checks are complete.

faq.question: What type of review file does this skill expect?
faq.answer: It expects a Markdown review document with severity tags, locations, problem descriptions, and proposed fixes.

faq.question: Does it commit code changes?
faq.answer: No. It updates files and review status only. A separate pre-commit or commit workflow should run afterward.

faq.question: Can it preview work before editing?
faq.answer: Yes. Dry-run mode shows the issues and proposed work without modifying source files.

faq.question: Which severities does it understand?
faq.answer: It prioritizes BLOCKING, then SHOULD_FIX, then NIT findings.

faq.question: Is auto mode safe for any review document?
faq.answer: No. Auto mode should be used only with trusted review documents after confirming expected target files.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, and uses general file, edit, and shell workflows.
